authority.note: This packet frames required adversarial reviews; script generation never answers or decides them.

limitations: Evidence context is assembled mechanically and may include irrelevant rows; the reviewer must judge relevance.
A pending red-team prompt is not a judgment_review and cannot support an M6 decision.
No script-authored verdict or recommendation is permitted.
Priority weights allocate review attention only.
Later judgment must preserve Commander-first identity and bracket-specific context.

reviews.adversarial_challenge: Assume multiple permanent types are answered over several turns. Identify which strategic routes actually rebuild and which collapse after repeated removal.

audit_focus.card: Brass's Tunnel-Grinder // Tecutlan, the Searing Rift

value: Don't become generic Grixis reanimator: the targets should be Pirates the commander can return.
Don't self-mill as an end in itself.
Revel in Riches-style off-plan alternate wins were cut for commander synergy (source decision).

blueprint_failure_modes.description: Graveyard exile (Bojuka Bog, Rest in Peace) shuts off the commander and mass reanimation.
Finality counters mean each reanimated Pirate is usually exiled the next time it would die.
Commander ETB mill and self-mill may hit lands or non-Pirates.

value.interaction: Graveyard hate is the main threat; keep stack interaction to protect the reanimation turn.
value.protection: Greaves, Stormtamer and free protection for the commander.

accepted_role.advances_plan: Brass's combat trigger is a free Pirate reanimation every turn; the self-mill and Pirate-ETB choices exist for it.
accepted_role.honest_note: Finality counters exile the returned Pirate when it would die, so each card is usually a one-shot unless Power Conduit removes the counter; the engine slowly consumes the graveyard.

reviews.question: Can the deck rebuild after repeated removal across multiple permanent types?
